reference: GNU coreutils chgrp for private file metadata with the GID already owned by the fixture; no users, authentication, capabilities or group memberships change. Bash help/type are metadata contracts.
coverage: Numeric existing-group application, symlink default/-h, multiple paths with a missing middle file, missing operands and unknown group.
Bash registration and documented help metadata only for the metadata cases.
-R recursion with the default -P, -H and -L symlink traversal, and -f
Guest pass 5 (G74/G78): GNU long options, abbreviations and diagnostics, and the -c/-v/-d/-I/--reference behaviours of coreutils 9.7.
Clean-room rewrite: operand forms, report wording, traversal modes, --from/--reference, --preserve-root and option scanning against GNU coreutils 9.7.
exclusions: Changing to distinct GIDs and controlled named-group resolution remain deferred for a disposable VM or syscall mock.

cases.purpose: Confirm through Bash's documented type -t interface that the statically compiled chgrp name is registered as a builtin, without invoking it.
Check the synopsis registered for chgrp using Bash's help -s builtin interface; this checks metadata only.
Check Bash's long help text against the documented chgrp description and usage line, without running an ownership operation.
cases.stdout:
chgrp: chgrp GROUP FILE...
    Change file group.
    
    chgrp [OPTION]... GROUP FILE...   GROUP is a name or numeric id.
    chgrp [OPTION]... --reference=RFILE FILE...

cases.purpose: Compare a valid named group, an unknown group name, and a numeric group ID against GNU using a controlled group database; verify status and resulting metadata for successful calls.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable VM or resolver/chown syscall mock with synthetic group mappings and distinct permitted GIDs. Current cases only reapply the existing group of private fixture files; no account database is modified.

cases.purpose: Apply the existing fixture GID to two private files and verify contents and mode preservation.
cases.script:
printf private > data
gid=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; print(os.stat("data").st_gid)')
printf second > other
chmod 640 data
chgrp "$gid" data other
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; a=os.stat("data"); b=os.stat("other"); assert a.st_gid == b.st_gid; print(oct(a.st_mode & 0o777), open("data").read())'

cases.purpose: Exercise default and -h symlink policy using the already-owned GID, preserving the private link and target.
cases.script:
printf private > data
gid=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; print(os.stat("data").st_gid)')
ln -s data link
chgrp "$gid" link
chgrp -h "$gid" link
[[ -L link ]]

cases.purpose: A missing middle file reports failure while valid neighbors use an already-owned fixture GID.
cases.script:
printf private > data
gid=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; print(os.stat("data").st_gid)')
printf tail > after
chgrp "$gid" data missing after

cases.purpose: Compare a missing-operand error rejected before any file ownership syscall.
An unknown group is rejected without changing the private file.
cases.script:
printf private > data
chgrp fixture-group-that-does-not-exist data

cases.purpose: chgrp -R walks a nested tree containing an internal dangling symlink; the default -P changes the link itself.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub/deep
printf 'b\n' > tree/sub/deep/b
ln -s missing-target tree/sub/dangling
chgrp -R runner tree
printf 'ok\n'

cases.purpose: -R -H follows a symlink named on the command line into its directory.
cases.script:
mkdir -p real/sub
printf 'x\n' > real/sub/x
ln -s real link
chgrp -R -H runner link
printf 'ok\n'

cases.purpose: chgrp -v and -c describe each file as GNU does; --reference, --recursive and GNU diagnostics (G74, G78).
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
: > a; : > b; mkdir -p d/e
n chgrp -v runner a
n chgrp -c runner a
n chgrp --verbose --recursive runner d
n chgrp --reference=b -v a
n chgrp -v "$(/usr/bin/id -g)" a
n chgrp -v 0 a | s
n chgrp -v nosuchgroup a | s
n chgrp -v runner | s

cases.purpose: GROUP operand forms: names, numbers, a leading '+', blanks before a number, the empty operand (no change), and GNU's invalid-group diagnostics (chgrp has no OWNER or '.' forms).
chgrp reports: 'group of ... retained as', refused changes, missing files, -c/-f, --from and --reference.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
g=$(/usr/bin/id -g)
: > a; : > b
n chgrp -v 0 a | s
n chgrp -c 0 a | s
n chgrp -vf 0 a
n chgrp -cf 0 a
for grp in runner 0 '' "+$g"; do n chgrp -v -- "$grp" nosuch | s; done
for f in 0 runner runner: :runner :0 ''; do n chgrp -v --from="$f" runner a | s; done
n chgrp --from=nosuch x | s
n chgrp --from=runner.runner -v runner a | s
n chgrp -v --reference=b a
n chgrp -v --reference=nosuch a | s
n chgrp --reference=b | s
n chgrp runner | s
n chgrp --re runner a | s

cases.purpose: chgrp -R with -P, -H and -L, -h and --dereference, dangling links (-c keeps GNU's unspecified 'from' text out of the comparison), an unreadable directory and --preserve-root.
cases.script:
n(){ "$@" 2>&1 && echo rc=0 || echo "rc=$?"; }
s(){ sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //'; }
g=$(/usr/bin/id -g)
mkdir -p t d/e u/locked; : > t/f; : > d/x; ln -s ../t d/lt; ln -s ../t/f d/lf; ln -s nosuch d/dl; ln -s d ld; ln -s / lroot
for o in -R -RH -RL -RLh -RHh "-RL --dereference"; do echo "== $o"; n chgrp -c $o runner ld | s; done
n chgrp -Rv runner ld | s
n chgrp -RHhv runner ld | s
n chgrp -RLhv runner ld | s
n chgrp -R --dereference runner d | s
chmod 000 u/locked
n chgrp -Rv runner u | s
chmod 700 u/locked
n chgrp -RH --preserve-root runner lroot | s
n chgrp -R --preserve-root -v runner lroot
